title: End-to-end ingestion corridor for OSS LLMs: deterministic conversion, pin generation, and perf-profile publishing
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a resilient, auditable pipeline that accepts open-source model weights (community/registry), performs deterministic conversion to our runtime format, runs a minimal safety and smoke validation, generates a canonical version pin, and publishes a performance profile to the model catalog. The corridor must be observable, idempotent, and support fast rollback semantics if a pinned variant regresses in downstream evals.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Pipeline accepts a declared manifest (s3/tar/registry link) and emits an ingest artifact with provenance metadata.
2) Conversion step produces deterministic runtime artifacts for CPU/GPU-compatible formats (float16 + int8 candidates) and records conversion checksums.
3) Automated smoke validation passes: end-to-end sample generation, KV-cache sanity, and tokenization parity.
4) Profiling: generate latency and throughput profiles (p50/p95, tokens/sec) for canonical sequence lengths and publish profile JSON and artifact to catalog.
5) Pin generation: create immutable version pin (pin:<hash>:<variant>) with metadata linking profile and conversion artifacts.
6) Canary: new pins must route 1% traffic in dedicated staging cluster and run evaluation harness for 24 hours before allowing >1% promotion.
7) Observability: per-run telemetry published to DataDog/Grafana; failures surface as incidents and attach to onboarding run.
8) Rollback: a single command reverses pin publish and reverts routing in under 10 minutes.
9) Documentation: README, runbook, and audit trail stored in Confluence and attached to the model catalog entry.
comments: 2025-01-16 - Ava Chen: Kickoff + design review scheduled. Initial scope: manifest schema, conversion container, deterministic checksum strategy. Asked infra to reserve staging cluster for canary runs.

2025-01-20 - Diego Martinez: PoC conversion container completed. Supports transform from HF checkpoint -> runtime tar; uses reproducible file ordering and header canonicalization to make outputs deterministic. Noted a race in protobuf timestamps; introduced normalization layer. PR opened: #412.

2025-01-23 - Priya Natarajan (ML): Ran early profiling on 7B and 13B community weights. Observed p95 tail dominated by context init for long sequences; proposed KV cache warmup shim in runtime. Decision: include a warmup token-run in smoke validation to get realistic latency numbers. Recording in design doc.

2025-01-28 - Liam O'Connor (Infra): Canaries provisioned in eu-west-1 staging pool. Autoscaling policy for 1% traffic stated but needs limits to avoid noisy neighbor impacts. We will add burst-limiter and soft quota per onboarding run.

2025-01-31 - Diego Martinez: Integration test failure: quantized int8 candidate produced mismatched logits on a deterministic prompt (diff > 1e-3). Trade-off discussion: tighten quantization calibration (per-layer min-max) or mark int8 as experimental and exclude from immediate pin. Proposal: publish float16 canonical pin and attach int8 experimental variant tag. Seeking approval.

2025-02-02 - Ava Chen: PM review feedback: ensure model catalog UI receives both 'canonical' and 'experimental' flags and that release notes are auto-generated from run metadata. Also request that audit logs include operator ID and triggering event (manual/auto).

2025-02-03 - Diego Martinez: Work in progress — converting canary promotion flow into a state machine (pending -> canary -> promoted | rejected). Implemented promotion API; tests for rollback hooks in flight. Next: finalize runbook and add auditing to S3 artifact storage (server-side encryption, HSM KMS key), coordinate security review.
2025-02-03 - Priya Natarajan: Flagged evaluation harness for hallucination and toxicity checks must be included in the canary stage. Added evaluation suite ticket to PM backlog.
2025-02-03 - QA (Elena Park): Added acceptance test: 'profile reproducibility' which re-runs profiling three times to ensure variance < 3% for p50 on staging hardware.
